subject: general
question: The vast network of railways that helped people meet their family and relatives was pioneered during the latter half of which of the following centuries in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**19th century**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The vast network of railways** that connected people and helped them meet their families and relatives was pioneered in India during the **latter half of the 19th century**.
 
• The introduction of railways in India was initiated by the British colonial government for administrative, economic, and strategic purposes. *Hence, the correct option is the 19th century.*
 
• The first railway line in India was opened in **1853**, connecting **Bombay (Mumbai)** to **Thane**. This marked the beginning of modern transportation in India. 
 
• Railways played a crucial role in the **industrial and economic development** of India during the 19th century, facilitating the transportation of goods, raw materials, and people over long distances.
 
• The development of railways was aligned with the British Empire’s interest in ensuring smooth governance and quick access to resources across their territories in India. 
 
• By the end of the 19th century, India had a **well-established railway network** that connected major cities and towns, laying the foundation for the modern railway system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Development of Railways in India:**

 
 
• **1853:** The first railway line was inaugurated, connecting **Bombay (Mumbai)** to **Thane** with a distance of 34 km.
 
• The British government aimed to use railways for **economic exploitation**, administrative efficiency, and military purposes.
 
• The railways also facilitated the transportation of **raw materials** like cotton, jute, and tea from India to Britain.
 
• By the end of the 19th century, the railway network in India had expanded significantly, connecting major cities like **Calcutta (Kolkata), Delhi, and Madras (Chennai)**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Railways during the 19th Century:**
 
 
• The railways served as a crucial mode of **transportation for goods and people**, enabling trade and commerce.
 
• It helped in integrating different regions of India, fostering **social and cultural exchanges**.
 
• The introduction of railways also contributed to the **urbanization** of India by connecting rural areas to urban centers.
 
 
 
• **Global Significance:**
 
 
• The railway system in India was one of the largest in the world during the 19th century, showcasing the British Empire’s focus on infrastructure development in colonies.
 
• It laid the groundwork for India’s modern transportation system, which continues to be a vital part of the country’s economy today.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significant Railway Milestones:**

 
 
• The railway system in India was developed largely with the investment and expertise of British engineers and companies.
 
• By the end of the 19th century, India had more than **40,000 km** of railways, making it one of the largest networks in the world.
 
• The establishment of railways in India marked the beginning of modern infrastructure development and greatly influenced the country’s economy and society.
